name: Golden Teacher
summary: Common cubensis strain. Reference conditions for research and education only.
notes: Informational climate only. Not a cultivation guide for illegal activity.
chamber_notes: Cubensis typically uses a tub/casing workflow the Shrooly does not replace. This only covers humidity, temperature, light, and fresh air.
legal_notice: Psilocybin mushrooms are illegal to grow, possess, or sell in most countries and under US federal law. This information is published for educational, research and harm-reduction purposes only. Check the laws where you live. Shroom Labs does not sell spores, cultures or psilocybin products.

source_notes.title: Chamber consensus
source_notes.detail: Community fruiting-chamber consensus (Roger Rabbit / Shroomery-style tek ranges), cross-checked with vendor cards. P. cubensis colonizes ~24 to 27 °C; pins and fruits ~21 to 24 °C at high humidity with 12/12 light.

source_notes.title: Practice
source_notes.detail: Fresh air is increased at pinning. Surface should be fine droplets, not standing water.

stages.name: Colonization
stages.notes: Dark, still. Do not add fresh air early.

light_recipe.why: Badham 1980 showed P. cubensis initials need light, with peaks at 370, 440, and 460 nm. McKernan 2023 fruited at 12 h. Intensity is the labeled general default (20% white / 92 lux) because those papers do not give a room lux.
light_recipe.wavelength_note: WS2812 blue is roughly 465 to 475 nm. The RGB mix is an approximation of cited wavelengths, not a measured spectrum.

sources.title: Badham 1980
sources.detail: Edmond R. Badham, The Effect of Light Upon Basidiocarp Initiation in Psilocybe cubensis, Mycologia 72 (1980). Initials formed only after light. 370, 440, and 460 nm were effective. Wavelengths longer than 510 nm were not. The saturating dose is a flash energy, not a room lux, so intensity here is the general default.

sources.title: McKernan et al. 2023 fruiting protocol
sources.detail: Kevin McKernan et al., Exploring Psilocybe spp. mycelium and fruiting body chemistry, PLOS ONE (2023). Fruiting used a 12 h photoperiod at about 6400 K. No lux number.

sources.title: Sakamoto 2018
sources.detail: Yuichi Sakamoto, Influences of environmental factors on fruiting body induction, development and maturation in mushroom-forming fungi, Fungal Biology Reviews 32 (2018). Light is a fruiting cue for many basidiomycetes. Blue light is the usual photomorphogenesis signal. Agaricus bisporus is called out as not needing light for a cap. Flammulina velutipes can fruit in the dark as a long stem with a tiny cap.

sources.title: General default
sources.detail: No variety-specific photoperiod or lux was found for this species. Colonization is dark (Sakamoto 2018; Penn State oyster spawn run). Fruiting uses 12 h (Stamets) and 20% white, which is 92 lux on this chamber, inside the Penn State oyster 50 to 300 lux band. Blue 80% approximates the 440 to 470 nm finding. This is a labeled default, not a measured value for this variety.
